tweets.author: btconchainassistan.bsky.social
tweets.text:
On-chain data and technical indicators on Bitcoin don't always agree.

When they don't, we say so — instead of blending both into one tidy verdict that hides the disagreement.

tweets.author: btconchainassistan.bsky.social
tweets.text:
4-hour, daily and weekly Bitcoin analysis — each one labeled with its real time window.

We'll never call a 4-hour reading "the trend" for the next month. A different timeframe is a different question, not a bigger claim.

tweets.author: btconchainassistan.bsky.social
tweets.text:
Every AI-written explanation we publish about Bitcoin — chat replies, weekly digests, even automated emails — carries a visible "Generated by AI" marker.

Not because a law will require it soon. Because you should always know when you're talking to a machine.

tweets.author: btconchainassistan.bsky.social
tweets.text:
When one of our Bitcoin data sources fails, we don't quietly show you yesterday's number as if it were new.

We show "no data available yet" instead. A gap in the feed, never a stale figure pretending to be real-time.

tweets.author: btconchainassistan.bsky.social
tweets.text:
A "92/100, bullish" score sounds precise. It's made up — nobody can compress 9 Bitcoin on-chain indicators and up to 11 technical ones into one honest number.

We count them instead: how many are low, neutral, or high. No fake score. No single verdict.
